newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crude business waits for VLCC plays.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crude business waits for VLCC plays.

text.p: Foreign crude business into the U.S. was subdued Friday, with domestic players waiting to see where North Sea barrels set for December import land.
One of the pair of VLCC's fixed for December 21 and 25 loading dates was confirmed sold for delivery to the U.S. Gulf. Other barrels coming over have yet to find homes.
"We'll get more information on those barrels next week," said a trader.

Widening arbitrage for trans-Atlantic barrels attracted some interest from at least one Wall Street house, and other players. The spread, on the screen, between January West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent was around $1.10-$1.15 a barrel for most of Friday.
Spread levels were squeezed late after the January IPE Brent rallied ahead of the NYMEX on expiration-inspired buying, traders said.
The strong rally on the IPE failed to stop a drift lower in North Sea crude premiums.
Dated Brent was offered as low as 15 cents below January Brent paper, down from even and +20 cents the previous two sessions.
Mediterranean grades were off as well, making themselves cheaper on the completion of five crude contracts contracts this week under the U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food deal.

Coastal Corp was believed to be a holder of one of the five contracts okayed by the United Nations this week. The firm was expected to take 60,000 barrels per day (bpd) to its refinery on the Caribbean island of Aruba, sources have said.
In the U.S. aftermarket, dealings were slim and featured a trade for a full cargo of February Brent paper at $22.95, 4 cents higher than the IPE settlement price.
